title: Non-pressure ulcer depth and burn extent
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the ulcer, or for the burn extent (T31) when the note is about a burn (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Scald burns.

Vitals:
T: 98.4 F, BP: 132/78, HR: 76 (RRR), RR: 16, SpO2: 97% on RA.

Recent Labs:
WBC: 8.2, Hgb: 12.4, Hct: 38, Na: 138, K: 4.1, Cl: 102, BUN: 18, Cr: 0.9, eGFR: >90.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Denies fever or chills.
Integumentary: Pain and erythema to burned areas.
MSK: No joint pain or swelling.
Neuro: Alert and oriented x3.
Other systems: NAD.

Social History:
Lives at home with daughter. Retired. Non-smoker.

Family History:
Mother: Hypertension.
Father: Heart disease.

Hospital Course:
Pt is an 85-year-old female admitted for management of scald burns. Initial assessment showed burns covering 15% of the body surface area. Of these areas, 5% were identified as third degree, requiring specialized wound care. Pt was managed in the acute care unit. Treatment focused on wound debridement, irrigation, and application of antimicrobial dressings. Pain managed with scheduled analgesics. Wound status improved over the course of stay. Pt tolerated diet well and remained hemodynamically stable. Dressing care was demonstrated to pt and daughter prior to discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
- Scald burns of body surface (15% BSA)
- Third degree burns (5% BSA)

Discharge Medications:
- Acetaminophen 650mg BID PRN pain
- Bacitracin ointment to burns BID
- Cephalexin 500mg BID x7 days

Follow-up:
F/u with wound clinic in 7 days for dressing change and evaluation.

Electronically signed
D. Kowalski, MD
05/18/2026
explanations: Burns of 10-19% of the body with under 10% third degree: T31.10 (no HCC).
